examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
A PMF assigns nonnegative point masses summing to one. A PDF integrates to one; its height is not a point probability. The CDF F(x)=P(X≤x) is nondecreasing, right-continuous and tends to zero/one at the extremes. Its jump size equals a point mass. The identity P(a<X≤b)=F(b)−F(a) works for discrete and continuous laws, but changing endpoint inclusions matters at atoms.

**Key relationship:** P(a<X≤b)=F(b)−F(a); P(X=x)=F(x)−F(x⁻)

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Identify support and type.
2. Normalize masses or density.
3. Use CDF differences with correct endpoints.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: A PMF assigns point probabilities; a PDF integrates to probabilities and is not itself a point mass. Normalize before solving for a constant. The CDF F(x)=P(X≤x) is nondecreasing and right-continuous; jump sizes give discrete point probabilities. For a continuous variable, P(X=x)=0 even where its density is positive.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
X has density f(x)=cx on [0,2] and zero elsewhere. Find P(1≤X≤2).

**Answer: 0.75.** Normalization gives c·∫₀²x dx=2c=1, so c=1/2. The requested integral is (1/2)·[x²/2]₁²=3/4=0.75.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A density can exceed 1 over a short interval; its integral over the entire support must be 1. Discrete and continuous probability rules cannot be mixed without specifying the distribution.

For continuous variables, a nonzero density at x does not mean P(X=x)>0.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

P(X=0)=0.3,P(X=2)=0.7. Find F(1).

- **A.** 0
- **B.** 0.3
- **C.** 0.7
- **D.** 1

**Answer: B.** Only the mass at zero lies at or below one, so F(1)=0.3.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Every CDF is:

- **A.** Nondecreasing
- **B.** Right-continuous
- **C.** Always differentiable
- **D.** Between zero and one

**Answer: A, B, D.** A/B/D are universal. Discrete CDFs have jumps and need not be differentiable.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

P(X=k)=ck for k=1,2,3. Find c.



**Answer: 0.16666566666666666 to 0.16666766666666666.** Normalization gives c(1+2+3)=1, so c=1/6.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2025 CS1 · Q58 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/random-variables?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Random variables, PMFs and CDFs. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Normalize the density: 1=C∫₁⁴x²dx=C(64−1)/3=21C, giving C=1/21.
2. The required probability is (1/21)∫₂³x²dx=(1/21)(27−8)/3=19/63.
3. Numerically 19/63≈0.301587, which rounds to **0.302**.

#### GATE 2025 CS2 · Q64 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/random-variables?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Random variables, PMFs and CDFs. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Put s=α+β and p=αβ. Equality of the polynomial with its squared-root version requires s=α²+β²=s²−2p and p=p², so p∈{0,1}.
2. If p=0, s=0 or 1 gives polynomials x² and x(x−1). If p=1, s²−s−2=0 gives s=2 or −1, yielding (x−1)² and x²+x+1.
3. Two of the four polynomials have repeated roots. Uniformly choosing among them gives **0.5**.
